actual_disk_region_geometry.claim: Let F be the compact connected smooth oriented genus-g surface with two boundary components, equipped with product endpoint collars and a chosen w-interval on each boundary. Choose interior points of these intervals. A path between them can be chosen piecewise smooth in finitely many coordinate disks. Remove its finite self-intersection loops after a transverse perturbation in the surface, then smooth the remaining corners; arrange it to be the collar-coordinate interval near both endpoints. This gives an embedded proper smooth arc a joining DIFFERENT boundary components.

A sufficiently thin closed regular neighborhood W of a, together with the chosen short endpoint boundary intervals, is a smooth disk with four sides: the two endpoint w-intervals and two dividing arcs. The surface orientation gives the ribbon orientation, so the cyclic side order is bottom w-interval, one dividing arc, top w-interval, other dividing arc. There is no interior ribbon vertex or arbitrary cyclic-order choice. The dividing arcs separate W from Z=closure(F−W); the boundary z-intervals lie in Z.

Z is connected. In a path in F, each transverse crossing of a can be detoured along one side of a to the lower boundary component, around that boundary away from its unique endpoint interval, and back along the other side. Because a has only one endpoint on that boundary component, that detour avoids a and joins the two sides. Thus paths between any two points of the complement can be chosen in the complement. Removing a thin neighborhood has the same connectedness. Cutting an arc joining distinct boundary components merges the two old boundary circles into one; hence Z has one boundary circle.

F=W∪Z and W∩Z is the pair of dividing intervals, so Euler additivity gives −2g=chi(F)=1+chi(Z)−2. Therefore chi(W)=1 and chi(Z)=1−2g. With one boundary component, Z has genusg. Thus a disk w-region and complementary genus-g z-region are actually available, independently of a movie presentation or any claim about map nonvanishing.

After forgetting the surface completely, choose a as the ribbon graph spine of W; W deformation retracts to it while the two marked endpoint intervals retract to their marked points. This graph is just a bare proper smooth arc in S3×I. Root and top_concordance_repair confirm reuse of the accepted bare-arc theorem smooth branch: after endpoint points are aligned, a can be straightened to the vertical product arc by an ambient isotopy relative the supplied endpoint collars. This statement has no adapted surface-strip, complement germ, annulus-isotopy-inverse or surface-straightening consequence.
